answer.headline: MIA has the longest CY2025 seat-weighted stage length of the four named Florida airports
answer.body:
For CY2025, seat-weighted average stage length on departing segments was {F3} at Miami International (MIA), {F2} at Orlando International (MCO), {F1} at Fort Lauderdale Hollywood International (FLL), and {F4} at Tampa International (TPA). Each value is {F3.class}, defined as {F3.definition}, and covers {F3.period} from {F3.source}.

MIA is the longest of the four. It is {F5} longer than MCO ({F10} higher) and {F8} longer than TPA ({F11} higher). MCO, FLL, and TPA sit much closer together: MCO is {F6} longer than FLL, FLL is {F7} longer than TPA, and the full span from MCO to TPA is {F9}. The gap from MIA down to MCO is {F12} times that MCO-to-TPA span.

claims.text: In CY2025, seat-weighted average stage length was {F3} at MIA, {F2} at MCO, {F1} at FLL, and {F4} at TPA. These are {F1.class} values for {F1.period}.

The order is MIA, then MCO, then FLL, then TPA. MIA exceeds MCO by {F5} and TPA by {F8}. MCO exceeds FLL by {F6}, and FLL exceeds TPA by {F7}. Relative to MCO, MIA is {F10} higher; relative to TPA, MIA is {F11} higher. The span from MCO to TPA is {F9}.
MIA is set apart from the other three named airports. The MIA-to-MCO gap ({F5}) is {F12} times the entire span from MCO to TPA ({F9}), while the steps among MCO, FLL, and TPA are {F6} and {F7}.

assumptions: The comparison set is exactly the four airports named in the question. MIA resolved only to Miami International Airport, MCO only to Orlando International Airport, TPA only to Tampa International Airport, and FLL only to Fort Lauderdale Hollywood International Airport. Each is in Florida with FAA hub class L.
Primary Florida airports is read as that named list. Other Florida commercial airports are outside this comparison.
limitations: The metric is seat-weighted average stage length on T-100 departing segments for all carriers, domestic and international. It is not passenger-weighted stage length, and it is not the catalog long-haul share.
Unmet demand, terminal capacity, fares, and profitability are not measured by this comparison, and these data do not establish why the stage lengths differ.
The figures are calculated from observed seats and distance for the full calendar year CY2025. They are not forecasts or estimates.
